# Overview

This notebook is the statistics-and-figures stage of the RSM (Response Surface
Methodology) experiment. A fungal culture was grown across a 7×7 design of
incubation time (days) × culture volume (mL) — 49 samples, one per photographed
colony — and the notebook integrates three kinds of measurement per sample into
the paper's figures, tables and models.

**Inputs** (resolved relative to this experiment's folder, no absolute paths):
from `data/raw/`, three spreadsheets — fresh biomass & pH
(`Exp1_biomass_pH.xlsx`), the glucose microplate assay (`Exp1_glucose.xlsx`), and
fresh-to-lyophilised biomass (`Exp1_fbm2lyo.xlsx`, used in the supplementary
section); and from `data/processed/grey_values/`, the per-colony grey-value files
(`Results*.jpeg.csv`), which are the output of the ImageJ macro
`Script_imageJ_Exp1`.

**Outputs**: figures to `results/figures/` and tables to `results/tables/`
(`Exp1 - Glu.csv` mean glucose per sample, `Exp1 - BM & GV.csv`, and
`Exp1 - Master datatable.csv`).

**Before running**: paths are portable via `here()` (anchored by the `.here`
file at the repo root), so nothing is machine-specific.

Packages and directories — load the packages the notebook uses and build every
input/output path relative to the repository.

```{r deps-and-paths, include = FALSE}
# 1. Dependencies
# Clear the workspace so a rerun starts from a known-empty state - no stale
# object from a previous run can silently feed into the results below.
rm(list = ls())
# All packages and the shared plotting theme are defined once in
# shared/dependencies.R and sourced from there, so a clean clone reproduces
# without editing this notebook. The script installs any missing packages,
# then attaches them. here::here() resolves the path from the .here file at
# the repo root; bootstrap the here package itself first in case it is missing.
if (!requireNamespace("here", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("here")
source(here::here("shared", "dependencies.R"))

# 2. Paths - portable, no machine-specific locations. here() finds the repo root
# (marked by the .here file) and builds every path from this experiment's folder.
# If you rename/move the experiment folder, update the two names in here() below.
base           <- here::here("experiments", "Experiment_1")
path.raw       <- file.path(base, "data", "raw")                       # measured inputs: spreadsheets + images/
path.processed <- file.path(base, "data", "processed")                 # generated & regenerable: ImageJ CSVs + intermediate tables
path.gv        <- file.path(base, "data", "processed", "grey_values")  # the ImageJ Results*.jpeg.csv files
path.figures   <- file.path(base, "results", "figures")                # final paper figures (ggsave)
path.tables    <- file.path(base, "results", "tables")                 # final paper tables

```

## DATAFRAMES

Read the measured spreadsheets and build the working dataframes the rest of the
notebook draws on.

BIOMASS: my_df

`my_data` is the master measured table: one row per Time × Volume sample, holding
fresh biomass (FBM), dry biomass (DBM) and pH. Most of the notebook builds on it —
grey value and glucose are joined onto it later.

```{r load-biomass, echo=FALSE}
my_data <- read_excel(file.path(path.raw, "Exp1_biomass_pH.xlsx")) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# factor version of the same data, convenient for grouped plots/stats
my_df <-  my_data %>%
  mutate(Volume = as.factor(Volume),
         Time = as.factor(Time))
```

GREY VALUE: my_gv_df

Grey value is the mean pixel brightness of each colony — a proxy for biofilm
opacity/transmittance (denser film → lower grey value). The `Results*.jpeg.csv`
files are the ImageJ macro's output, so here that processed result becomes this
notebook's input.

Load data

```{r}
#### GREY VALUE
# point path.raw at the ImageJ CSV folder for the reads below
path.raw <- path.gv
path.figures <- file.path(base, "results", "figures")
path.tables <- file.path(base, "results", "tables")

csvs <- list.files(path.raw, pattern = "*.jpeg.csv")
# csv is a single-file handle kept only for interactively testing csv_read();
# the pipeline below maps csv_read() over all of csvs, so this line is optional.
csv <- csvs[1]

```

Generate function to process

`csv_read()` reads one ImageJ Results file and keeps the mean grey value. Each
colony's Time and Volume aren't stored inside the file — they're encoded in its
name — so the function parses them out of the filename and returns them as
columns, giving every reading its Time/Volume coordinates.

```{r}
csv_read <- function(csv) {
  df <- read.csv(csv, sep = ",") %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.integer), as.numeric)) %>%
    select(Mean) %>%
    # extract the part after "Results" and before ".tif.csv" / ".jpeg.csv"
    mutate(origin = str_extract(csv, "(?<=Results)\\d+_.*(?=\\.tif\\.csv|\\.jpeg\\.csv)")) %>%
    separate(origin, into = c('date', "experiment", "time", "volume"), sep = "_") %>%
    # strip any file extension left on the volume token
    mutate(volume = str_remove(volume, "\\..*$")) %>%
    select(time, volume, Mean)
  return(df)
}
```

Apply function to files

The RSM design is a 7×7 grid — 7 culture volumes × 7 incubation times = 49
samples. The `volumes`/`times` vectors hold the real-world values; the V1–V7 and
t1–t7 labels in the filenames are indices into them, so the lookups convert each
index back to its actual mL / day.

```{r}
volumes <- c(18, 36, 54, 72, 90, 108, 126)
times <- c(7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14)
my_volumes <- paste0(volumes, " mL")

# csv_read() reads by bare filename, so move into the CSV folder first
setwd(path.raw)
df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(csvs, csv_read))
my_gv_df <- df %>%
  mutate(timeN = as.factor(str_extract(time, "\\d+")),
         volumeN = as.factor(str_extract(volume, "\\d+")),
         Volume = as.numeric(volumes[volumeN]),
         Time = as.numeric(times[timeN])) %>%
  arrange(Volume)
```

GLUCOSE: my_dfA

Glucose was quantified on 96-well microplates over two assay runs (sheets 1 and
2). Each sheet stores three aligned blocks — optical density, the sample design,
and the dilution factors — read out by cell range below and combined into glucose
concentrations.

Load data

```{r}
# per sheet: B1:M8 = OD readings, B13:M21 = sample design, B25:M34 = dilutions
my_plate1A <- as.data.frame(read_excel(file.path(base, "data", "raw", "Exp1_glucose.xlsx"), range = "B1:M8", sheet = 1))
my_design1A <- as.data.frame(read_excel(file.path(base, "data", "raw", "Exp1_glucose.xlsx"), range = "B13:M21", sheet = 1))
my_dilution1A <- as.data.frame(read_excel(file.path(base, "data", "raw", "Exp1_glucose.xlsx"), range = "B25:M34", sheet = 1))
my_plate2A <- as.data.frame(read_excel(file.path(base, "data", "raw", "Exp1_glucose.xlsx"), range = "B1:M8", sheet = 2))
my_design2A <- as.data.frame(read_excel(file.path(base, "data", "raw", "Exp1_glucose.xlsx"), range = "B13:M21", sheet = 2))
my_dilution2A <- as.data.frame(read_excel(file.path(base, "data", "raw", "Exp1_glucose.xlsx"), range = "B25:M34", sheet = 2))
```

Calibration curve

The first three columns of plate 1 are a standard series of known glucose
concentrations (a further 10× dilution applies). Averaging their triplicate OD
readings and regressing OD on concentration gives the slope used to convert
sample OD into glucose concentration.

```{r}
cc_conc <- c(2, 1, 0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.2, 0)
my_df_cc <- as.data.frame(my_plate1A[,1:3])
dil_curve <- 10
my_cc <- my_df_cc %>%
  mutate(conc = cc_conc,
         mean = rowMeans(across(c(`1`, `2`, `3`))),
         new_conc = conc/dil_curve)

# "+ 0" forces the fit through the origin (zero glucose -> zero signal)
model <- lm(mean ~ new_conc + 0, data = my_cc[1:8,])
r2 <- summary(model)$r.squared
coefs <- coef(model)

eq_label <- sprintf("y = %.4fx + 0, R2 = %.4f", coefs[1], summary(model)$r.squared)

## Calibration curve A plot
cc_plot <- ggplot(data = my_cc[1:5, ], aes(x = new_conc, y = mean)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, label = eq_label, hjust = 3.2, vjust = 2)
cc_plot
```

OD converted to glucose concentration

Reshape each plate block to one row per well, merge OD with its design and
dilution, then convert OD to glucose concentration using the calibration slope
and each well's dilution. Both runs are processed the same way.

```{r}
## Plate 1 run A
# reshape each block (OD / design / dilution) to long form, one row per well, for merging
my_val <- my_plate1A[,4:12] %>%
  mutate(row = row_number()) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -row, names_to = "Column", values_to = "value_num") %>%
  mutate(Sample = paste0(row, "_", Column)) %>%
  as.data.frame()

my_des <- my_design1A[,4:12] %>%
  mutate(row = row_number()) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -row, names_to = "Column", values_to = "value_des") %>%
  mutate(Sample = paste0(row, "_", Column)) %>%
  as.data.frame()

my_dil <- my_dilution1A[,4:12] %>%
  mutate(row = row_number()) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -row, names_to = "Column", values_to = "value_dil") %>%
  mutate(Sample = paste0(row, "_", Column)) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# merge the three blocks on the well key; Conc = OD x slope / in-curve dilution x well dilution; column 4 is a blank
my_df1A <- Reduce(function(x, y) merge(x, y, by = c("row", "Column", "Sample")),
                  list(my_val, my_des, my_dil)) %>%
  filter(if_all(everything(), ~ !is.na(.))) %>%
  mutate(Plate = 1, Run = "A",
         value_dil = as.numeric(value_dil)) %>%
  mutate(Conc = (value_num * coefs[1])/dil_curve*value_dil) %>%
  filter(!Column == 4)


## Plate 2 run A
my_val <- my_plate2A %>%
  mutate(row = row_number()) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -row, names_to = "Column", values_to = "value_num") %>%
  mutate(Sample = paste0(row, "_", Column)) %>%
  as.data.frame()

my_des <- my_design2A %>%
  mutate(row = row_number()) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -row, names_to = "Column", values_to = "value_des") %>%
  mutate(Sample = paste0(row, "_", Column)) %>%
  as.data.frame()

my_dil <- my_dilution2A %>%
  mutate(row = row_number()) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -row, names_to = "Column", values_to = "value_dil") %>%
  mutate(Sample = paste0(row, "_", Column)) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# merge the three blocks on the well key; Conc = OD x slope / in-curve dilution x well dilution; column 4 is a blank
my_df2A <- Reduce(function(x, y) merge(x, y, by = c("row", "Column", "Sample")),
                 list(my_val, my_des, my_dil)) %>%
  filter(if_all(everything(), ~ !is.na(.))) %>%
  mutate(Plate = 2, Run = "A",
         value_dil = as.numeric(value_dil)) %>%
  mutate(Conc = (value_num * coefs[1])/dil_curve*value_dil)
```

Merge databases

Combine both plates into one glucose table. The design label (e.g. `t3v5`)
encodes Time after "t" and the volume index after "v"; the three column-groups of
the plate are the technical replicates, decoded here into Techrep 1–3.

```{r}
## Merge both dataframes
volumes <- c(18, 36, 54, 72, 90, 108, 126)
times <- c(7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14)
my_volumes <- paste0(volumes, " mL")

my_dfA <- bind_rows(my_df1A, my_df2A) %>%
  mutate(Time   = as.numeric(str_extract(value_des, "(?<=t)\\d+")),
         Volume = as.numeric(str_extract(value_des, "(?<=v)\\d+")),
         Volume = volumes[Volume],
         value_dil = as.numeric(value_dil),
         Techrep = as.factor(case_when(Column == 1 | Column == 4 | Column == 7 | Column == 10 ~ 1,
                                       Column == 2 | Column == 5 | Column == 8 | Column == 11 ~ 2,
                                       Column == 3 | Column == 6 | Column == 9 | Column == 12 ~ 3)),
         Sample = as.factor(paste0(Time, "_", Volume)),
         Sample_Tech = as.factor(paste0(Sample, ".", Techrep))) %>%
  #arrange(Sample_Tech, desc(Run == "A")) %>%
  #distinct(Sample_Tech, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample, Sample_Tech, Techrep, Time, Volume, value_num, Conc)
```

Stats for glucose consumption (n = 3)

Average glucose per sample across the three technical replicates, written to
`results/tables/` as `Exp1 - Glu.csv`, alongside the other output tables. The
correlations section below takes glucose straight from `df_rsm_stats` in memory,
so this file is an output rather than a dependency.

```{r}
df_rsm_stats <- my_dfA %>%
  group_by(Sample, Time, Volume) %>%
  summarise(meanC = mean(Conc), sdC = sd(Conc)) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::select(Volume, Time, meanC) %>%
  arrange(Volume, Time)
#write.table(df_rsm_stats, file = file.path(path.tables, "Exp1 - Glu.csv"), dec = '.', sep=",", row.names = F)

```



## Fresh biomass and GV

Overlay dry biomass (points, at their true values) and lnGV (bars) for the 108 mL
series on one dual-axis plot. Because grey value falls as biomass rises, lnGV is
mapped into biomass space with a negative slope so the two line up; the secondary
axis inverts that mapping.

```{r}
str(my_data)   # quick structure check (console only, not part of any figure)
my_gv_df$lnGV <- log(my_gv_df$Mean)
# select by position: my_gv_df cols 6,7,8 = Volume, Time, lnGV
gv_df <- my_gv_df[,c(6,7,8)]
# my_data cols 4,5,7 = Volume, Time, FBM (Volume + Time are the join keys)
fbm_df <- my_data[,c(4,5,7)]
# join grey value onto biomass by the shared Volume + Time columns
fbm_gv_df <- left_join(gv_df, fbm_df)
fbm_gv_df_108 <- fbm_gv_df[fbm_gv_df$Volume == 108,]

fbm_rng <- range(fbm_gv_df_108$FBM)    # ~3.6 .. 9.1
gv_rng  <- range(fbm_gv_df_108$lnGV)   # ~4.30 .. 5.06

# map lnGV -> FBM space with a NEGATIVE slope:
#  gv_max -> fbm_min, gv_min -> fbm_max
b <- -diff(fbm_rng) / diff(gv_rng)
a <-  fbm_rng[1] - b * gv_rng[2]

y_bottom <- fbm_rng[1] - 0.2           # base the bars sit on (bottom of window)

# NOTE: this standalone theme() call is a no-op - it is not added to a plot nor
# set via theme_set(), so it has no effect. The theme actually applied is the
# one inside the ggplot() below; this block only documents the intended legend.
theme(
    legend.position      = "right",
    legend.justification = "bottom"   # vertically centred, same height as the axis title
  )

FBM_lnGV <- ggplot(fbm_gv_df_108, aes(x = Time)) +
  # bars = lnGV mapped into FBM space, rising from the bottom
  geom_segment(aes(x = Time, xend = Time, y = y_bottom, yend = a + b * lnGV,
                   colour = lnGV),
               linewidth = 10, lineend = "butt") +
  # points = FBM at their TRUE values on the primary axis
  geom_point(aes(y = FBM),
             shape = 21, size = 3, stroke = 0.6,
             fill = "#FFF7B2", colour = "black") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name     = "Dry biomass (g)",                                # FIRST axis  = FBM (left)
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ (. - a) / b, name = "Transmittance")   # SECOND axis = GV (right)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    name     = "Time (days)"
  ) +
    scale_colour_viridis_c(
    option = "inferno", direction = -1, name = NULL,   # no title
    transform = "sqrt",
    limits = c(4, 5.1),
    oob = scales::squish,
    guide = guide_colourbar(reverse = TRUE)
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position      = "right",
    legend.justification = c(-1, 0)   # aligns the legend to the bottom of the right margin
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(y_bottom, fbm_rng[2] + 0.2))

FBM_lnGV

#ggsave(file.path(path.figures,"1. Exp1_FBMtoTransmittance.svg"), FBM_lnGV, width=12, height=8, units="cm", scale=1.15)
```

## PLOT fresh biomass

Contour plot of fresh biomass over the Time × Volume grid. The 49 values are
reshaped into the 7×7 grid the contour geom expects (the same reshape is reused
for the grey-value and pH maps). A single `contour_panel()` helper, defined here
and reused by all three figures, draws the filled contour and carries its own
continuous colourbar — so each map is one self-contained ggplot object with no
separate legend plot to generate and align.

```{r}
# 3. Prep for ggplot
xlabel = "Incubation time (days)"
ylabel = "Total volume (mL)"

df_contour <- expand.grid(
  times   = unique(my_data$Time),
  volumes = unique(my_data$Volume)
)

# Helper: one contour map with its own continuous colourbar, so each figure is a
# single ggplot with no companion legend plot. geom_contour_filled() draws the
# filled bands; mapping fill to the numeric band midpoint it computes
# (after_stat(level_mid)) with a continuous scale colours each band to its exact
# value on the colourbar. `value` is the df_contour column to map (already
# log-transformed where needed); direction = -1 reverses the ramp (grey value);
# rescaler warps the data -> colour mapping (default linear; grey value passes an
# exponential ramp - see the grey-value chunk).
contour_panel <- function(df, value, fill_name, direction = 1, rescaler = scales::rescale) {
  ggplot(df, aes(x = times, y = volumes, z = .data[[value]])) +
    geom_contour_filled(aes(fill = after_stat(level_mid)), bins = 25) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "inferno", direction = direction, name = fill_name,
                         rescaler = rescaler) +
    labs(x = xlabel, y = ylabel) +
    theme(panel.border = element_blank()) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = unique(my_data$Volume))
}

# 4. Fresh biomass contour plot
# byrow = F fills column-major: each column is one Volume across the 7 Times,
# matching df_contour = expand.grid(times, volumes) where times vary fastest.
matrix_FBM <- matrix(unlist(my_df$FBM), nrow = 7, ncol = 7, byrow = F)
df_contour$FBM <- as.vector(matrix_FBM)

graph_fresh_biomass <- contour_panel(df_contour, "FBM", "FBM (g)")
graph_fresh_biomass
#ggsave(file.path(path.figures, "2. Exp1_FBM.svg"), graph_fresh_biomass, width=7.5, height=6, units="cm", scale=1.5)

```



## PLOT gray value

Grey Value

Contour of grey value (log scale) over the Time × Volume grid, built with the same
`contour_panel()` helper.

```{r}
# 6. Grey value plot
matrix_GV <- matrix(unlist(my_gv_df$Mean), nrow = 7, ncol = 7, byrow = F)
df_contour$GV <- as.vector(matrix_GV)
df_contour$lnGV <- log(df_contour$GV)   # grey value is displayed on a log scale

# direction = -1: denser biofilm -> lower grey value, so reverse the colour ramp.
# Exponential ramp (k = 3): hold full yellow only at the lowest grey values and
# darken quickly, so mid/dark tones dominate the map (u = linear 0-1 position).
gv_ramp <- function(x, to = c(0, 1), from = range(x, na.rm = TRUE)) {
  u <- (x - from[1]) / (from[2] - from[1])
  (1 - exp(-3 * u)) / (1 - exp(-3))
}
graph_GV <- contour_panel(df_contour, "lnGV", "Grey Value", direction = -1, rescaler = gv_ramp) +
  guides(fill = guide_colourbar(reverse = TRUE))   # invert the bar: yellow (low grey value) on top
graph_GV
#ggsave(file.path(path.figures, "3. Exp1_lnGV.svg"), graph_GV, width=7.5, height=6, units="cm", scale=1.5)

```


## MODEL FOR BIOMASS FORMATION

The response-surface model: a full second-order (quadratic) regression of fresh
biomass on Time and Volume with both squared terms and their interaction — this is
what "RSM" refers to. The fitted surface is then used to locate the Time/Volume
that maximises biomass.

Model

```{r}
Volume <- as.numeric(my_data$Volume)
Time <- as.numeric(my_data$Time)
Biomass <- my_data$FBM

# model
my_model <- lm(Biomass ~ Time + Volume + I(Time^2) + I(Volume^2) + Volume:Time)
summary(my_model)
```

Analytical point of time and volume where biomass is maximized

```{r}
# solve for the surface's stationary point: A is the Hessian (2nd-order coeffs),
# cvec the linear terms; -solve(A, cvec) is the maximising Time/Volume
b <- coef(my_model)
A <- matrix(c(2*b["I(Time^2)"], b["Time:Volume"], b["Time:Volume"], 2*b["I(Volume^2)"]), nrow = 2)
# gradient's linear terms: the model has both a linear Time and a linear Volume
# coefficient, so both belong here. b["Volume"] is ~0 and non-significant, but
# including it keeps the stationary point exactly consistent with the fitted model.
cvec <- c(b["Time"], b["Volume"])
stationary <- -solve(A, cvec)
stationary
```

Analytical maximum biomass

```{r}
# set plot boundaries
time_min <- 0
time_max <- 30
vol_min <- 0
vol_max <- 300
resolution <- 100

# calculate max biomass
Time_g <- seq(time_min, time_max, length = resolution)
Vol_g <- seq(vol_min, vol_max, length = resolution)
grid <- expand.grid(Time = Time_g, Volume = Vol_g)
max(predict(my_model, newdata = data.frame(Volume = grid$Volume, Time = grid$Time)))
```

Prepare axis and lims of plot

```{r}
# create grid
Time_g <- seq(min(Time), max(Time), length = resolution)
Vol_g <- seq(min(Volume), max(Volume), length = resolution)
grid <- expand.grid(Time = Time_g, Volume = Vol_g)

# make matrix
grid$yhat <- predict(my_model, newdata = data.frame(Volume = grid$Volume,
                                                    Time   = grid$Time))
grid$yhat <- ifelse(grid$yhat > 0.15, grid$yhat, 0)
z <- matrix(grid$yhat, nrow = resolution)
# diagnostic print (unassigned): grid rows lying near the stationary Time
grid[grid$Time > stationary[1] - 0.2 & grid$Time < stationary[1] + 0.2, ]
z_norm <- (z - min(z)) / (max(z) - min(z))
```

Plot biomass in plotly

Interactive 3-D surface of predicted biomass over the Time × Volume space.

```{r}
# Plot biomass
fig <- plot_ly(x = Time_g, y = Vol_g, z = z, type = "surface",
               # 49 discrete colours = one per sample in the 7x7 design
               color = z, colors = viridis_pal(option = "B")(49)) %>%
  layout(scene = list(xaxis = list(title = "Time"),
                      yaxis = list(title = "Volume"),
                      zaxis = list(title = "Biomass"))) %>%
  add_surface(contours = list(z = list(show=TRUE, usecolormap=TRUE, project=list(z=TRUE))), showscale = T) %>%
  # TODO: "My Plot Title" is a placeholder - set the figure's real title or drop it
  layout(title = list(text = "My Plot Title",
                    font = list(size = 22)))
fig
```

Resolve equation for biomass

Predicted biomass at the experimental points, expanded term by term from the
model coefficients.

```{r}
# Predicted biomass at the experimental points. Use predict() so this reproduces
# the fitted model exactly (including the linear Volume term).
Biomass_hat <- predict(my_model)
```

## PLOT glucose

Reducing-sugar concentration versus incubation time, one line per culture volume.
Both layers draw from `df_rsm_stats` (per-sample means): black lines with line type
encoding Volume, and points coloured by concentration. The base `ggplot()` is seeded
with `my_dfA` only to set up the axes.

```{r plot-glucose, echo=FALSE}
# one line type per volume
linetypes_ordered <- c("solid", "dotted", "dotdash", "longdash", "twodash", "dashed", "solid")

my_plotA_inferno <- ggplot(my_dfA, aes(x = as.numeric(Time), y = Conc)) +
  labs(y = "Reducing sugars (g/L)", x = "Incubation time (days)") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(7, 14, by = 1)) +
  # Lines with linetype by Volume
  geom_line(data = df_rsm_stats, aes(x = as.numeric(Time), y = meanC, group = as.factor(Volume), linetype = as.factor(Volume)),
    linewidth = 1, inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "black") +
  # Points filled by meanC
  geom_point(data = df_rsm_stats, aes(x = as.numeric(Time), y = meanC, colour = meanC),
    shape = 16, size = 3) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "inferno", direction = -1, name = "Conc") +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = linetypes_ordered, breaks = volumes, name = "Volume") +
  ylim(0, 9) #+
  #theme(legend.position = "bottom")

my_plotA_inferno
```

## GLUCOSE MODEL

Fit glucose against incubation time and volume using only the pre-peak samples
(the same per-volume time cut-offs as the grey-value/biomass correlation). `Surface`
and `MGlucose` are per-volume constants attached for the alternative model
formulations tried below.

Dataframe

```{r}
## Glucose consumption linear model
# Self-contained: join per-sample mean glucose (df_rsm_stats$meanC) onto the numeric
# biomass table by Volume + Time, so this section is independent of the `glu` column
# in the CORRELATIONS section below. Volume/Time stay numeric, so the
# lm below fits continuous slopes (as the eq_label assumes), then keep the pre-peak
# time points per volume (cut-offs below).
my_glulm_df <- dplyr::left_join(my_data, dplyr::rename(df_rsm_stats, glu = meanC),
                                by = c("Volume", "Time"))

my_surfaces <- c(49.43, 49.85, 50.26, 50.67, 51.08, 51.49, 51.90)
my_glucose <- c(0.59, 0.88, 1.06, 1.20, 1.30, 1.46, 1.36)
my_lm_df <- my_glulm_df[my_glulm_df$Volume == volumes[1] & my_glulm_df$Time %in% times[1:2] |
                        my_glulm_df$Volume == volumes[2] & my_glulm_df$Time %in% times[1:3] |
                        my_glulm_df$Volume == volumes[3] & my_glulm_df$Time %in% times[1:5] |
                        my_glulm_df$Volume == volumes[4] & my_glulm_df$Time %in% times[1:6] |
                        my_glulm_df$Volume == volumes[5] & my_glulm_df$Time %in% times[1:7] |
                        my_glulm_df$Volume == volumes[6] & my_glulm_df$Time %in% times[1:7] |
                        my_glulm_df$Volume == volumes[7] & my_glulm_df$Time %in% times[1:7],] %>%
  mutate(Surface = c(rep(my_surfaces[1], 2), rep(my_surfaces[2], 3), rep(my_surfaces[3], 5), rep(my_surfaces[4], 6), rep(my_surfaces[5], 7), rep(my_surfaces[6], 7), rep(my_surfaces[7], 7)),
         MGlucose = c(rep(my_glucose[1], 2), rep(my_glucose[2], 3), rep(my_glucose[3], 5), rep(my_glucose[4], 6), rep(my_glucose[5], 7), rep(my_glucose[6], 7), rep(my_glucose[7], 7)))
                     

```
Model — an additive Time + Volume fit (common slope) compared against a
Time × Volume interaction; the additive model is kept as `my_model`.

```{r}
# additive (common-slope) model kept as my_model; the my_model1 reassignments try
# alternative predictors - only the last (Time * Volume) survives for the anova.
my_model <- lm(glu ~ Time + Volume, my_lm_df)
my_model1 <- lm(glu ~ Time + Surface, my_lm_df)
my_model1 <- lm(glu ~ Time + MGlucose, my_lm_df)
my_model1 <- lm(glu ~ Time + MGlucose + Surface, my_lm_df)

summary(my_model)
my_model1 <- lm(glu ~ Time * Volume, my_lm_df)
summary(my_model1)
anova(my_model, my_model1)
r2 <- summary(my_model)$adj.r.squared
coefs <- coef(my_model)

my_volumes <- paste0(volumes, " mL")

my_lm_df$pred <- predict(my_model)
```
Plot — fitted glucose lines from the additive model, over the measured points.

```{r}
eq_label <- sprintf("y = %.4f + %.4ft + %.4fv, R2 = %.4f", coefs[1], coefs[2], coefs[3], r2)

linetypes_ordered <- c("solid", "dotted", "dotdash", "longdash", "twodash", "dashed", "solid")

sugar_model_plot <- ggplot(my_dfA, aes(x = as.numeric(Time), y = Conc)) +
  labs(y = "Reducing sugars (g/L)", x = "Incubation time (days)") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(7, 14, by = 1)) +
  geom_line(data = my_lm_df, aes(x = Time, y = pred, group = as.factor(Volume), linetype = as.factor(Volume)),
            linewidth = 1, inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "black") +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "inferno", direction = -1, name = "g/L") +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = linetypes_ordered, breaks = volumes, name = "Volume") +
  geom_point(data = df_rsm_stats, aes(x = as.numeric(Time), y = meanC, colour = meanC, shape = as.factor(Volume)), size = 3) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(7:12, 14), breaks = volumes, name = "Volume") +
  ylim(0, 9)
  #annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, label = eq_label, hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.5)
sugar_model_plot
#ggsave(file.path(path.figures, "5. Exp1_glu_model.svg"), sugar_model_plot, width=8, height=7, units="cm", scale=1.5)

```


## PLOT pH

Contour of pH over the Time × Volume grid, built with the same `contour_panel()`
helper and the same 7×7 reshape used for the biomass and grey-value maps.

```{r}
# 8. pH contour plot
# byrow = F, matching the FBM and GV reshapes above: my_df$pH is in the same row
# order as my_df$FBM, so both must fill the matrix column-major to land each
# value on its correct Time x Volume coordinate. (This was byrow = TRUE, which
# transposed the pH grid relative to the biomass and grey-value contours.)
matrix_pH <- matrix(unlist(my_df$pH), nrow = 7, ncol = 7, byrow = F)
df_contour$pH <- as.vector(matrix_pH)

graph_pH <- contour_panel(df_contour, "pH", "pH")
graph_pH
#ggsave(file.path(path.figures, "4. Exp1_pH.svg"), graph_pH, width=7.5, height=6, units="cm", scale=1.5)
```

Fermentative parameters

Standard bioprocess parameters per sample: dry biomass (FBM × 0.16), biomass
concentration Cx (g/L), productivity Qx (per hour), substrate-uptake rate Qs (from
glucose consumed against 20 g/L initial), and biomass yield on substrate Yxs.

```{r}
fp_df <- my_data %>%
  select(Volume, Time, pH, FBM, DBM, GV, glu) %>%
  rename(GBM = DBM,
         Glucose = glu) %>%
  mutate(Biomass = FBM * 0.16,
         LnGV = log(GV),
         Cx = Biomass / (Volume / 1000),
         Qx = Cx / (Time * 24),
         # 20 = initial glucose (g/L), so (20 - Glucose) is the amount consumed
         Qs = (20 - Glucose) / (Time * 24),
         Yxs = Cx / (20 - Glucose)) %>%
  select(Volume, Time, pH, LnGV, Biomass, Glucose, Cx, Qx, Qs, Yxs)
#write.table(fp_df, file = file.path(path.tables, "Exp1 - Master datatable.csv"), dec = '.', sep=",", row.names = F)
```

Culture height

Convert each culture volume to its liquid height in the vessel and compare the
theoretical, recalculated (`calc`) and measured heights.

```{r}
### From mL to cm
volumes <- c(18, 36, 54, 72, 90, 108, 126)
heights <- c(0.3656, 0.7282, 1.0878, 1.4445, 1.7983, 2.1492, 2.4974)
```

From fresh to lyo

Fit the fresh → dry (lyophilised) biomass relationship that underpins the 0.16
factor used in the fermentative parameters above, from the "3 - fresh to lyo"
sheet of `Exp1_fbm2lyo.xlsx`. Note: this chunk OVERWRITES `my_data`, so run it
last (or restart before rerunning the notebook from the top).

```{r}
# portable path (was a hardcoded absolute path); the spreadsheet is a measured input in data/raw/
my_path <- file.path(base, "data", "raw")
my_data <- read_excel(file.path(my_path, "Exp1_fbm2lyo.xlsx"), sheet = "3 - fresh to lyo") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  filter(!(Inc_day == 10 & Replicate %in% c(2, 4, 5, 6, 8)))

str(my_data)   # quick structure check (console only)

# "+ 0" forces the fit through the origin (zero fresh biomass -> zero dry biomass)
model <- lm(Lbio ~ Fbio + 0, data = my_data)
r2 <- summary(model)$r.squared
coefs <- coef(model)

eq_label <- sprintf("DBM = %.4f FBM + 0, R2 = %.4f", coefs[1], summary(model)$r.squared)

FBMtoLyo <- ggplot(my_data, aes(Fbio, Lbio)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = F, colour = "black") +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, label = eq_label, vjust = 4, hjust = 1.6) +
  labs(y = "Lyophilized biomass (mg)",
       x = "Fresh biomass (mg)")
#ggsave(file.path(path.figures, "S. Exp1_FBMtoLyo.svg"), FBMtoLyo, width=8, height=6, units="cm", scale=1.5)
```
